theme: The widow and judge; the Pharisee and the tax collector; Zacchaeus
readingInstruction: Read Luke 18:1-19:27. Two parables about prayer, children brought to Jesus, a rich ruler, a blind man healed, and Zacchaeus. Chapter 19:10 is the key verse of the whole Gospel.
settingTheScene: Jesus is near the end of his journey. He is about to enter Jericho and then go up to Jerusalem. These chapters hold several of Luke’s best known scenes: the Pharisee and the tax collector, Zacchaeus, and the parable of the minas. They show who receives the kingdom: the humble, the childlike, the despised, and the seeking.
observation: “He told them a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray and not lose heart” (18:1).
“And will not God give justice to his elect, who cry to him day and night?” (18:7).
“God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” (18:13).
“For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted” (18:14).
“Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them, for to such belongs the kingdom of God” (18:16).
“What is impossible with men is possible with God” (18:27).
“Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today” (19:5).
“For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost” (19:10).
interpretation:
The widow and the unjust judge teach persistence. A widow keeps coming to a judge who neither fears God nor respects people, and finally he gives her justice because she wears him out. If even an unjust judge responds, how much more will God, who is just and loving, answer his chosen ones? The lesson is to pray always and not lose heart.

The Pharisee and the tax collector teach humility. The Pharisee stands and thanks God that he is not like other men. The tax collector stands far off, beats his chest, and says, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” Jesus says this man went down to his house justified. Justification comes through humble faith in God’s mercy, not through the record of our good deeds.

Parents bring infants to Jesus, and the disciples try to stop them. Jesus welcomes them and says the kingdom belongs to such as these, and that whoever does not receive it like a child will not enter it. Then a rich ruler asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus points him to the commandments, and then says to sell everything and follow him. The man goes away sad, for he is very rich. Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom. The bystanders ask, “Who then can be saved?” and Jesus answers, “What is impossible with men is possible with God.” Salvation is a miracle.

For the third time, Jesus speaks of his death in Jerusalem. The disciples do not understand. Outside Jericho, a blind beggar cries, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” The crowd tells him to be quiet, but he cries out louder. Jesus heals him, and he follows, glorifying God.

In Jericho, Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector and wealthy, climbs a sycamore tree to see Jesus. Jesus calls him by name and invites himself to his house. The crowd grumbles. Zacchaeus repents, gives half his goods to the poor, and repays fourfold anyone he cheated. Jesus says, “Today salvation has come to this house.” Then verse 10 summarizes his whole mission: “For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.” The parable of the minas follows, to correct the idea that the kingdom will appear at once. The King is going away, and his servants are to be faithful until he returns.
connection: Habakkuk 2:4 says the righteous shall live by his faith. Psalm 51:1-4 is the prayer of a broken sinner. Psalm 34:18 says the LORD is near to the brokenhearted. Isaiah 66:2 says God looks to the humble and contrite. Ezekiel 34:16 promises that God will seek the lost. Romans 3:21-26 explains justification by faith. Luke 15 gave three parables of the lost. 1 Timothy 1:15 says Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.
application:
Pray the tax collector’s prayer slowly, ten times: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner.”

Keep praying for the thing you have prayed about for the longest time. Do not lose heart.

Ask who the Zacchaeus is in your life, someone others have written off. Reach out to them.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to teach you to pray always and not lose heart.
Pray, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner,” and mean it.
Thank Jesus for receiving sinners like Zacchaeus.
